title: In-memory SQLite pool serves a separate empty database per connection under concurrency
evidence: src/main.rs:80 SqlitePool::connect("sqlite::memory:") with sqlx 0.8.6 default max_connections=10; table created once at src/main.rs:84 (init_db) on a single connection, but each additional pooled connection to sqlite::memory: is a SEPARATE database with no 'books' table -> intermittent 'no such table: books' / lost data once a second connection is spun up under load. Graded tests never hit this (each test at src/tests.rs runs sequential queries on one reused connection).
suggestion: Set max_connections(1) for the in-memory pool, or use a shared cache (sqlite::memory:?cache=shared with a keep-alive connection), or connect to a file-backed sqlite:books.db so all connections see the same schema/data.

title: Tests exercise raw SQL, not the HTTP handlers
evidence: src/tests.rs:3-24 setup_test_db builds a fresh pool and every test (e.g. src/tests.rs:28 test_create_book_success) issues SQL directly; none call create_book/list_books/get_book/update_book/delete_book or drive the axum Router, so handler-level behavior (validation branch main.rs:108-115, status codes, the pool footgun) is unverified.
suggestion: Add integration tests that spin up the Router (e.g. axum test / tower::ServiceExt oneshot) and assert HTTP status codes + JSON bodies end-to-end.

title: POST /books returns 200 instead of 201 Created
evidence: src/main.rs:104-142 create_book returns Json<Book> which serializes with HTTP 200; agent stdout (_agent_stdout.log) claims '201, 204' but only DELETE (main.rs:279 NO_CONTENT=204) uses a non-200 success code.
suggestion: Return (StatusCode::CREATED, Json(book)) from create_book to match REST conventions and the agent's own claim.
